# Project structure

**Generated by `node tools/generate-command-docs.mjs`.**

`bigaap init` creates one directory in your project:

```
.bigaap-analyzer/
├── project.json
├── preferences.json
├── accessibility-policy.json
├── fidelity-policy.json
├── stack-adapter.json
├── target-brief.json
├── README.md
├── workspaces/
├── history/
├── corrections/
├── defects/
├── outputs/
```

## Directories

| Directory | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `workspaces/` | One analysis workspace per reference. Captures, evidence and IR live here. |
| `history/` | Fidelity iterations, append-only. |
| `corrections/` | Correction records filed against claims. |
| `defects/` | Defect reports raised against the tool from this project. |
| `outputs/` | Generated artifacts. Projections of an IR, never sources. |

They are **empty** in a fresh project. `init` captures nothing and analyses nothing, so
there is no evidence to put in them yet — and a directory of plausible-looking placeholder
artifacts would be worse than an empty one.

## The two halves

| | Declared intent | Recorded evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lives in | the config files | `workspaces/`, `history/`, `corrections/` |
| Written by | you | a capture or an analysis |
| Changed by | editing the file | filing a correction |
| May state a fact about the reference | **no** | yes |

Keeping them apart is what makes a claim traceable. A configuration value that could become
a measured fact would be indistinguishable from one that was measured.

## Generated artifacts are projections

Everything in `outputs/` is projected from an IR and stamped with its hash. Editing one is
unsupported and detectable — `bigaap verify` fails on a hash mismatch. To change a claim,
file a correction and regenerate.
